acceptance: The equivalence tests pass under the leak guard in a shard run that includes them, with and without chdb installed
chdb is not added to the global ignore list unless a written reason shows the global cannot be restored
A test in test_stub_installer_isolation.py still shows the guard flags a real leak of this attribute
context: Failing in release canary runs 37798380568 (shard 1) and an earlier shard 2 run. The failing set changes day to day (4 tests on 2026-10-06, 9 on 2026-10-07, 3 on 2026-10-08), so confirm against a fresh canary run rather than the old list. Not reproducible locally in a quick run; reproduce under the shard's xdist settings.
description: The release canary fails in shards 1 and 2 with 'test leaked stub-installer state on adapter modules: benchbox.platforms.clickhouse._dependencies.chdb' on tests in tests/integration/platforms/test_tpchavoc_clickhouse_equivalence.py. The guard in tests/integration/platforms/conftest.py (find_stub_adapter_attr_leaks) reports the attribute because it is None when the snapshot is taken and the imported chdb module afterwards. This is a different attribute from the __warningregistry__ one fixed in the commit that added _IGNORED_LEAK_ATTRS, so that fix does not cover it. Prefer restoring the global in the test or its fixture (monkeypatch) over adding chdb to _IGNORED_LEAK_ATTRS, because an ignore entry would hide real leaks of the same attribute from later tests.
